name: Average speed over equal distances
formula: \bar v = \frac{\text{total distance}}{\text{total time}} = \frac{2uv}{u + v} \ \text{ for two equal legs at speeds } u, v
whenToUse: A trip has two parts of the same length at different speeds, such as there and back, and the question asks for the average speed.
example: Out at $30$ mph and back at $60$ mph gives $\frac{2 \cdot 30 \cdot 60}{30 + 60} = 40$ mph. Check with a $60$-mile leg: $2 + 1 = 3$ hours for $120$ miles is $40$ mph.
pitfall: Average speed is NOT the average of the speeds when the legs cover equal distances; the slow leg takes longer, so the answer is below $\frac{u + v}{2}$. Equal TIMES would give the plain average.
derivation: With each leg of length $d$, the total time is $\frac{d}{u} + \frac{d}{v}$, and $\frac{2d}{d/u + d/v} = \frac{2uv}{u + v}$, the harmonic mean of $u$ and $v$.
